entry.title: Get to know each twin
entry.summary: The Baby authors suggest using each child’s name and noticing their needs individually. Being the same age does not require treating the children as a single unit.
entry.cue: For families with twins, while getting to know what is particular to each child.
detail: Look at what each child is interested in and what help each needs. The authors suggest calling them by their names, rather than referring to them only as “the twins.”
They also describe involving both children in daily life as their skills grow. Their examples invite participation and taking turns; they do not require buying two of every toy.

The chapter recognizes the practical work of caring for two children of the same age. For example, it explicitly says that simultaneous breastfeeding may be possible and is also okay if it is not manageable. This is an acknowledgment of family capacity, not a feeding instruction.

references.locator: Individual names and needs, gradual participation, toy turns and adult capacity

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
